newsitem.title: USA: Mass. top court says parent okay needed for abortion.
newsitem.headline: Mass. top court says parent okay needed for abortion.

text.p: Massachusetts highest court Tuesday ruled that teenagers who seek abortions must get the approval of one parent instead of both as the state's law originally required.

In a 4-2 ruling, the state's Supreme Judicial Court modified Massachusetts' law that required anyone 18 years of age or younger seeking an abortion to get the approval of both parents or seek authorisation from a judge.

The 16-year-old law was one of the most restrictive parental consent laws in the country, according to the Planned Parenthood League of Massachusetts (PPLM), which brought the lawsuit hoping to eliminate all parental approval for the procedure.
"We are reservedly pleased with this decision, which eases one of the most restrictive minors consent laws in the United States," said Nicki Nicholas Gamble, PPLM president.

The Massachusetts Citizens for Life, Inc., an anti-abortion group, said the ruling "is good news for those who respect the fundamental rights of parents to protect the well-being of their minor daughters."
